links.note: Toy-scale CHECK of a closure derivation. Mathematical research on planted discrete logs on toy curves only; no deployed key. Not a performance race.

question: Does the reading of an ECDLP instance as (E,Q)=<k>(E,P) in a (Z/N)^*/+-1 torsor over one point of X_0(N) carry any computable structure beyond scalar multiplication? Specifically: (a) is the diamond action exactly (E,P)->(E,kP) with a free rational orbit of (N-1)/2 points, (b) do Hecke T_ell (ell=2,3) and the Eichler-Shimura relation leave the fibre coordinate invariant (forced-zero discrepancy), (c) does a single F_p-valued fibre coordinate behave like a random map, and (d) does the degree of the explicit separating functions grow like N^2 and stay above N^(1/2) for N>=37?

claims.text: For every toy instance (E,P,Q=kP), the Tate-normal-form point of (E,Q) equals the diamond image <k>(E,P): an explicit isomorphism certificate carries (E,kP) to (b,c)(k) and the (N-1)/2 orbit forms are pairwise distinct and F_p-rational (free action, F1/F2 of IDEA-20260806-0c9de1).

For every F_p-split ell-isogeny (ell in {2,3}) from each toy curve, the transported logarithm log_{phi(P)} phi(Q) equals k, T_ell(E,Q)=<k>T_ell(E,P) as sets of Tate pairs, the X_0 labels of the neighbours coincide for P and Q, and Verschiebung gives V(P)=[p mod N]P (F3). Discrepancy count is exactly zero.

The number of colliding pairs among {b(E,aP)}, a=1..(N-1)/2, is consistent with the random-map null (uniform draws from F_p), so a single F_p-valued fibre coordinate leaks no structure (F2: single-point invariants carry nothing). Planted-structure positive control (x(aP), a=1..N-1) must be detected.

Measured degrees of the explicit separating functions b and c on X_1(N) (N prime, 5..47) are at least the Kim-Sarnak/Abramovich lower bound 0.004959*(N^2-1) for N>=37 where the bound is rigorous, exceed N^(1/2) for all N>=19, and grow with log-log slope within [1.7,2.3].

Hopping to one rational ell-isogenous neighbour before the orbit lookup does not lower the counted cost of recovering k relative to the plain Tate-orbit lookup by more than the A/A spread (it adds the isogeny overhead).
claims.if_supported: descriptive statement on these toy instances only; no scaling claim
claims.if_not_supported: a Hecke-hopped orbit is cheaper than the plain orbit by more than noise: reopen

claims.text: Characteristic-p gonality of X_1(N)_{F_p} is at least N^(1/2) when N is comparable to p. Kim-Sarnak covers characteristic 0 only, and specialisation can only lower gonality; this is the single proof obligation (PO-1) the toy check does not discharge.

hypotheses.statement: H0 (closure): the diamond/Hecke/Eichler-Shimura relations hold with zero discrepancy, single-coordinate collision counts match the random-map null, and every tested separating function has degree >= max(KS bound, N^(1/2)) with slope ~2. H1 (reopen): any discrepancy, any collision-count p-value at or below alpha/m, or any separating function of degree below N^(1/2) at N>=37 is found.
hypotheses.mechanism: Diamond operators commute with every Hecke correspondence and act freely and transitively on the fibre (Galois group (Z/N)^*/+-1); rational torsors with a rational point are trivial; gonality of X_1(N) grows with the index (N^2-1)/2.

predictions.minimum_effect: zero failures in all checked certificates (exact)
zero discrepancies over all F_p-split neighbours (>=30 neighbours required, else inconclusive)
empirical two-sided p > alpha/m = 0.05/6 for every N; positive control p <= alpha/m
deg(b),deg(c) > N^(1/2) for all N>=19 and >= 0.004959*(N^2-1) for N>=37; log-log slope in [1.7,2.3]

arms.description: Baby-step giant-step with the negation map, own counted group-op accounting; the matched reference that sets the sqrt(N) scale for calibration only
Diamond-orbit table: for a=1..(N-1)/2 form (b,c)(E,aP) and match against (b,c)(E,Q) (sign handled by (E,-P)=(E,P) in X_1(N)); the lead's best case for a computable fibre coordinate
Same lookup performed inside one F_p-split 2- or 3-isogenous neighbour (E',phi(P)); the Hecke-compatibility best case

parameters.ell: smallest ell in {2,3} with a split neighbour

arms.description: orbit-tate with the scan order reversed (descending a): nuisance factor only

Collision detector applied to x(aP), a=1..N-1, which carries exact planted structure (x(aP)=x(-aP) gives (N-1)/2 forced collision pairs); same code path as the b-collision test. Also: fibre coordinate cheaply recovered by orbit-tate at every N<=4001 (N small enough to enumerate), and degree detector fires at N in {5,7} where X_1(N) has genus 0 and the Hauptmodul d (b=d for N=5; b=d^3-d^2, c=d^2-d for N=7) has degree 1

Non-matching pairs: (E,P) against (E2,Q2) with E2 a different curve of the same prime order N (different j). Diamond, Hecke and orbit-lookup checks must report 'no relation' and the orbit lookup must exhaust all (N-1)/2 forms without a match

positive.expected_detection: collision test p<=alpha/m on the planted x(aP) map for all six N; orbit-tate recovers k up to sign in 100% of instances; degree detector (deg<=N^(1/2)) fires at N=5,7

null_population.description: pairs (E,P),(E2,Q2) with E2 non-isomorphic to E (different j) at the same prime order N
null_population.generator: E2 = next curve in the same-N list from the seed stream; Q2 uniform non-identity point of E2(F_p)
null_population.why_n: one non-matching partner per matching pair, so every check is run on 108 matched and 108 unmatched pairs
matched_on: scalar distribution of the discrete log

factors.name: N
factors.how: prime orders {101,251,509,1009,2003,4001}; degree check uses primes 5..47

factors.name: curve
factors.how: 6 curves per N, y^2=x^3+Ax+B over F_p, p prime near N (|p+1-N|<=2sqrt(p)), #E(F_p)=N exactly (cofactor 1), j-invariants pairwise distinct, from the seed stream; independent of arm

factors.name: planted_k
factors.how: 3 values per curve, uniform in [2,N-2], k != +-1, from the seed stream; independent of arm

factors.name: instrument
factors.value: one Rust binary, sha256 pinned at freeze
factors.how: all arms are subcommands of one binary

factors.name: threads
factors.how: single-threaded; counted metrics do not depend on it

factors.name: scan_direction
factors.how: A/A arm reverses the scan; baseline ascending

factors.name: host
factors.how: recorded per row; affects no counted metric and no clock is read

seed_derivation.note: seed(N,curve,k)=SHA256(protocol_sha256||'level-torsor'||N||curve_index||k_index); null-resample seed likewise; frozen before any data

instance_sampling.rule: per N, draw p, A, B from the seed stream until #E(F_p)=N prime and j is new; 6 curves; 3 planted k each; negative-control partner curve is the next curve in the same N list

blinding.how: checks are exact and unambiguous; the only statistical test (collision) is label-free

power.note: collision test: 20,000 add-one null resamples per N, minimum attainable two-sided p = 2/20001 ~ 1e-4 < alpha/m = 0.05/6 ~ 0.0083. Resolution only, not power: the exact checks (C1,C2,C4) have no sampling error, and the collision test is expected null, so its power against a real effect is not claimed; the positive control (exactly planted collisions) shows the detector can reject. 6 N x 6 curves x 3 k = 108 pairs; 36 curves for orbit/Hecke checks.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: not measured; design-time probes only (PARI elldivpol deg probe 0.2 s for N<=19; curve search at N=2003 0.1 s)

primary.name: diamond certificate failures
primary.definition: instances (and orbit forms) for which the independent checker rejects the isomorphism certificate, the orbit-size count (N-1)/2, distinctness or rationality

primary.name: Hecke discrepancies
primary.definition: neighbours (E',phi) with log_{phi(P)}phi(Q) != k, or T_ell set mismatch, or V(P) != [p mod N]P

primary.name: collision-count empirical p-value
primary.definition: two-sided add-one empirical p of the number of colliding pairs among (N-1)/2 values b(E,aP) against 20,000 resamples of the same number of uniform F_p draws, per N, pooling the 6 curves by summing counts
primary.formula: p = (1 + #{null resamples with collision count >= observed or <= mirrored tail}) / (20000 + 1), doubled smaller tail, capped at 1

primary.name: degree of b and c on X_1(N)
primary.definition: number of c (resp. b) roots, with multiplicity, of the order-N condition for the Tate curve at a fixed b0 (resp. c0) after removing discriminant factors, at two large primes and two parameter values that must agree

primary.name: counted cost in M-equivalents
primary.definition: mul=1, sqr=1, inv=10 (sensitivity at 5 and 20 reported), from the first target-dependent operation to the verified k, table construction and canonicalisation included; Tate conversion and isogeny evaluation charged by their real field-op tuples

secondary.name: split neighbours
secondary.definition: F_p-split ell-isogenies (ell=2,3) enumerated over the 36 curves

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 6 N x 6 curves x 3 k (108 pairs) for C1,C2,C3,C5; 13 primes N=5..47 for C4; then stop
fewer than 30 F_p-split neighbours in total makes C2 inconclusive; the ell list is NOT extended after the data are seen

invalidation_rules: a curve with #E(F_p) != N or a repeated j-invariant is re-drawn from the seed stream before any check runs
a degree whose two (prime, parameter) replicates disagree is flagged invalid_measurement and not used

decision_rule.text: Closure confirmed iff all hold: diamond_failures=0 and hecke_discrepancies=0 over >=30 neighbours; negative control reports no relation in 108/108 pairs; positive controls detect; collision p>alpha/m for all six N; function_degree meets P4; C-hecke ratio interval within [0.97,1.10]. REOPEN iff any decisive check fails in the direction stated in its prediction, in particular a separating function of degree below N^(1/2) at N>=37, any nonzero Hecke discrepancy, or a collision p<=alpha/m. A failed positive or negative control gives invalid_measurement, never closure.
decision_rule.threshold: exact checks: zero failures; collision: p>0.05/6; degree: >N^(1/2) for N>=19 and >=0.004959(N^2-1) for N>=37; cost ratio interval within [0.97,1.10] and A/A half-width below 0.03
decision_rule.statistic: sum of cost_m over instance pairs, ratio orbit-tate-hecke/orbit-tate
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed cost_m; collision-count difference from null mean in null standard deviations

collision count vs null per N

inadmissible: changing N, the ell list, seeds, the null law or the counted-unit weights after seeing results
reading the orbit-tate/bsgs-ref ratio as a scaling or speed claim: orbit enumeration costs (N-1)/4 expected steps by construction, so that comparison calibrates the unit and decides nothing
treating a function that merely evaluates cheaply (b, c are O(1) from (E,P)) as evidence: evaluation is not inversion, and reading k from two Tate pairs is the DLP itself
using a curve-only statistic (X_0 data, j, ell-neighbour j-multisets) as a signal: it is k-independent by construction (LEAD-STR-torsion-module-leak)
extending toy results to cryptographic N, or claiming PO-1 (characteristic-p gonality) from the characteristic-0 bound
accepting a toy exact-recovery of k as evidence about any N beyond the enumerated range
